jobs.title: Director, Data Enablement, Data Platforms
jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.

For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.

Role Summary:

As Director, Data Enablement, you will architect and evolve reusable enterprise platforms, tools, and services that help users and applications discover, understand, and securely consume trusted data products.

You will set technical direction for data portals, APIs, software development kits and consumption services; advance adoption across departments; and establish scalable operating practices, architecture standards and engineering excellence. Reporting details were not provided.

Accountabilities & Qualifications:

CPP Investments’ technology and data functions build secure, scalable enterprise capabilities that support investment, analytics, research and operational needs across the organization. The Data Enablement Team helps the organization derive value from enterprise data by delivering reusable platforms, tools and services, including the enterprise Data Portal, the FinSights BI Portal, low-latency consumption services, product governance capabilities and operational dashboards.

Accountabilities

Architect, design and evolve reusable Data Enablement services, with measurable outcomes for data discovery, access, trust and adoption
Engage users and stakeholders across departments to understand their needs, promote available services and shape a multi-quarter product roadmap
Design secure, resilient and scalable services using DevSecOps, automation, service-level objectives, observability and effective incident response practices
Develop high-level and low-level solution designs, including threat models where required, and obtain Architecture Review Board and Information Security approvals
Partner with Cloud Foundation, Data Foundation, domain teams and control functions to deliver solutions aligned with enterprise standards and platform guardrails
Establish architecture standards for portals, APIs, software development kits and consumption services that integrate with the Enterprise Data Fabric and data catalogue
Own the operating model for consumer enablement services while coaching Lead and Senior Engineers and strengthening delivery, engineering and operational excellence

What You Bring

10+ years of experience building and operating enterprise platforms or shared services, including web portals and API ecosystems
Strong experience with AWS cloud platform engineering, including networking, security, identity and access management, and multi-account environments
Expertise in API and service-based architectures, including REST or GraphQL, event-driven patterns, Neptune, OpenAPI standards, versioning, backward compatibility and resiliency
Hands-on experience with Infrastructure as Code and DevSecOps practices, such as Terraform, continuous integration and delivery, automated security controls and observability
Experience with solution architecture, platform governance, Architecture Review Board processes and Information Security engagement
Proven ability to lead cross-functional delivery, influence without authority, develop engineering talent and align stakeholders around measurable enterprise outcomes
Experience with structured data and schema processing; knowledge of semantic modelling, agentic frameworks, retrieval methods, vector search, container platforms or governed data-serving technologies is an asset. Relevant AWS certifications are preferred

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

Inclusion & Accessibility

CPP Investments is committed to equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud

CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.

CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.

jobs.title: VP, Engagement Strategy
jobs.description:
About Us

At BGBx
, we're driven by a simple idea: breakthrough thinking creates breakthrough impact. As an independent commercial solutions partner to pharmaceutical and life science companies, we bring together strategists, scientists, communicators, creatives, technologists, and data experts to tackle some of healthcare's most important challenges.

Our teams work across consulting and communications to help clients shape strategy, launch innovations, engage stakeholders, and drive meaningful results throughout the product lifecycle. The work is complex, fast-moving, and deeply connected to improving lives, creating opportunities for curious minds to make a real difference every day.

If you're energized by collaboration, inspired by innovation, and motivated by work that matters, you'll find a place to grow, contribute, and make a meaningful impact at BGBx.

Position Overview

The VP, Engagement Strategy turns brand strategy into connected omnichannel engagement.
This senior leader defines how audience insight, behavioral science, content, media, CRM, field engagement, technology, and measurement work together across the customer journey. The VP leads clients and integrated teams from insight through activation and optimization, while helping grow BGBx's Engagement Strategy capability.

Key Responsibilities

Engagement & Omnichannel Strategy

Lead audience-centered, behaviorally informed omnichannel strategies across HCP, patient, caregiver, payer, and other stakeholder audiences
Translate brand and business strategy into connected journeys, engagement architectures, channel roles, sequencing, triggers, and activation roadmaps
Define how content, media, CRM, field, social, experiential, and digital interactions work together to move audiences toward desired behaviors
Make clear strategic choices and tradeoffs that focus investment on the moments and interactions most likely to create impact

Audience, Content & Experience

Turn research, segmentation, behavioral data, cultural context, and market dynamics into actionable audience understanding
Identify the beliefs, motivations, barriers, decision pathways, and moments of receptivity that engagement must address
Shape content and experience strategy so each interaction has a clear role, purpose, call to action, and connection to what happens next
Maintain the strategic throughline as work moves from strategy into creative development, implementation, and optimization

Measurement & Optimization

Define engagement objectives, KPI frameworks, signal plans, and learning agendas
Design closed-loop approaches that use customer response and performance data to improve content, channels, sequencing, and future engagement
Turn performance findings into clear strategic implications and optimization recommendations

Client, Growth & Team Leadership

Serve as a trusted strategic partner to senior clients and lead executive presentations, workshops, and high-stakes strategic conversations
Lead engagement and omnichannel strategy for pitches, organic growth opportunities, and capability development
Manage, mentor, and develop strategists while raising the quality, consistency, and visibility of BGBx's Engagement Strategy offering

Qualifications

10+ years of relevant experience across engagement strategy, omnichannel strategy, experience planning, digital strategy, CRM strategy, integrated strategy, or related disciplines
Significant pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences experience, preferably in an agency, communications, or consulting environment
Proven ability to lead complex engagement strategy from audience insight and problem definition through activation, measurement, and optimization
Strong understanding of HCP and patient journeys and the strategic roles of media, CRM, digital, social, field engagement, data, analytics, experience design, and marketing technology
Fluency in how personalization, marketing automation, modular content, next-best action, and decisioning can support omnichannel engagement
Strong client leadership, facilitation, executive communication, and strategic storytelling skills
Experience leading pitches, growing client relationships, and managing or developing strategists
Working knowledge of pharmaceutical regulatory, privacy, consent, and compliance considerations

Preferred Experience

Experience across both HCP and patient engagement and across launch, growth, or mature brand challenges
Experience translating global strategy into locally relevant engagement approaches
Practical experience with advanced segmentation, dynamic personalization, closed-loop marketing, or AI-enabled planning and optimization
Experience building or evolving an engagement, omnichannel, digital, or experience strategy capability

Interview Process

Candidates will be invited to discuss two anonymized examples of work they personally led, including one demonstrating end-to-end omnichannel strategy. We are most interested in problem framing, strategic choices, cross-functional leadership, measurement, and impact. Confidential client information and unpaid speculative work are not required.

Salary Range:
$200,000 - $240,000 CAD

The salary range provided represents what a potential hire may expect to earn in this role at BGBx. Actual salary decisions will be influenced by several factors that we use to determine overall fit, including experience (both direct and indirect), education, training, demonstrated qualifications, and organizational need. Salary is only one component of the total rewards package offered at BGBx.

What We Offer

At BGBx, we invest in our people because exceptional talent drives exceptional work. We provide a competitive rewards package designed to support your health, well-being, professional growth, and life outside of work.

Our benefits package typically includes health care insurance, retirement plans, generous paid time off and holidays, wellness benefits, life insurance, learning and development opportunities, and other resources that support our employees throughout their careers. Additional benefits may be available based on your location. Beyond benefits, you'll find a culture built on collaboration, innovation, inclusion, and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on healthcare and the people it serves.

BGBx is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship status, sexual orientation, disability, veteran status or any category or class of person protected by law.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Finding the right finance leader for a stadium is about more than producing accurate financial statements. It's about finding someone who can thrive in a fast-paced, event-driven business where concert nights can run late, operational decisions happen in real time, and leadership teams rely on financial insight to drive strategy. This role is ideal for a senior finance leader who loves getting into the details, building strong teams, and turning complex financial information into a clear business story.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Finance of BC Place is an experienced business and people leader responsible for providing financial oversight, direction, and leadership across the organization. Working closely with the Finance team, senior leadership, and operational stakeholders, this role ensures best-in-class financial reporting, analysis, controls, and compliance while helping drive strategic business decisions.

This is a highly visible leadership role within a dynamic venue and events environment. No two days are the same at BC Place. One day you may be leading the annual budgeting process, negotiating financial terms within a major contract, or presenting forecast updates to executives. The next, you may be overseeing event settlements following a sold-out concert that wrapped long after most offices have turned off the lights.

The successful candidate is a strong accounting professional first and foremost. They bring deep technical expertise, exceptional analytical capabilities, and the ability to translate financial results into meaningful business insights. They are equally comfortable reviewing complex reconciliations, coaching a finance team, supporting negotiations, and presenting strategic recommendations to executives.

What You Will Do

Lead all day-to-day financial operations for the BC Place, including oversight and integration of shared services accounting functions.
Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and completeness of financial records across all departments.
Oversee general ledger management, account reconciliations, and month-end and year-end close processes.
Deliver accurate, timely, and meaningful financial statements and management reporting.
Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and long-range financial planning processes.
Provide detailed financial analysis, operational reporting, and business insights that support strategic decision-making.
Analyze operating trends, financial performance, and key business drivers to identify efficiencies, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
Oversee event settlement preparation, review, analysis, and presentation while ensuring accuracy and strong client relationships.
Manage recurring billings, accounts receivable performance, credit management, and revenue reconciliation activities.
Lead capital asset management activities, including additions, disposals, write-downs, and maintenance of the capital asset register.
Ensure payroll processes are completed accurately and on time through effective procedures, support, and training.
Manage the annual external audit process and maintain strong relationships with auditors and external stakeholders.
Maintain and continuously improve financial policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and maintain financial reporting in accordance with PSAB requirements.
Provide financial guidance on contracts, leases, supplier agreements, sponsorship agreements, and other commercial arrangements.
Support leadership with contract reviews, negotiations, and financial risk assessments.
Advise senior leaders on financial impacts, emerging issues, and opportunities affecting business plans and budgets.
Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and excellence.
Partner with leaders across the organization to support operational success, strategic initiatives, and long-term business objectives.
Be prepared to support an events-based operation where concert and event schedules may occasionally require evening work and late-night financial oversight.

What You Will Bring

CPA designation is required.
University degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related discipline. A combination of education and experience may also be considered.
7+ years of progressive finance and accounting leadership experience, ideally including Controller-level responsibilities.
Proven success leading and developing finance teams within complex, multi-stakeholder organizations.
Deep technical accounting expertise with strong knowledge of financial reporting, internal controls, and accounting standards.
Experience with PSAB reporting standards is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated excellence in financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and analytical reporting.
Advanced financial modeling and business analysis capabilities with a natural curiosity for understanding the "why" behind the numbers.
Experience leading month-end and year-end close processes in fast-paced operational environments.
Strong audit management experience and ability to ensure compliance while driving process improvements.
Experience managing capital assets, contract reviews, lease accounting, and financial implications of commercial agreements.
Exposure to risk management and contract negotiations is considered an asset.
Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to influence and build credibility with executives, operational leaders, clients, and external partners.
A collaborative leadership style paired with strong business judgment and decision-making skills.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
Comfortable working in an events-driven environment where business needs occasionally extend beyond traditional office hours.
Passion for building efficient processes, creating strong controls, and helping an organization make informed decisions through data and financial insight.

This is a unique opportunity for a finance leader who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, leading through complexity, and partnering with a business that operates at the intersection of live events, operations, and community impact. If you're a strong Finance leader ready for your next challenge, or an experienced finance director looking for a highly visible leadership role where your work directly influences organizational success, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Financial Officer

Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo | Fort McMurray, Alberta

Aplin is proud to partner with the Regional Municipality of Wood Buffalo (RMWB)
in the search for an accomplished and strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
to join its senior leadership team.

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the CFO will provide executive leadership across Financial Services, Procurement, and Assessment and Taxation. This is an opportunity for a forward-thinking financial executive to influence the Municipality's long-term financial strategy, strengthen governance, and contribute to a business-focused, accountable, and data-driven organization.

The successful candidate will be a confident and decisive executive who brings deep financial expertise, strong business acumen, and exceptional communication skills. They will demonstrate sound judgment, a collaborative leadership style, and the ability to navigate the complexity of a large public-sector organization while building credibility with Council, senior leadership, employees, and key stakeholders.

The Opportunity

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the CFO will:

Lead the Municipality's financial strategy, long-term planning, budgeting, financial reporting, and governance.
Provide strategic financial advice and recommendations to the CAO, Council, and senior leadership.
Oversee Financial Services, Procurement, and Assessment and Taxation, ensuring effective and accountable service delivery.
Champion operational excellence, financial sustainability, continuous improvement, and informed decision-making.
Build and lead high-performing teams while fostering collaboration, transparency, and accountability.
Present complex financial information clearly and confidently to Council and other stakeholders.

The Ideal Candidate

We are seeking an accomplished financial leader who brings:

A minimum of 15 years of progressive financial or corporate services leadership experience, including five years at a senior management level.
A CPA designation and a degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Strong financial acumen, strategic planning capabilities, and experience leading complex, multidisciplinary functions.
Knowledge of public-sector accounting standards, financial governance, and municipal administration.
Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex financial matters into clear, practical recommendations.
A collaborative, decisive leadership style and the confidence to operate effectively in a dynamic, politically sensitive environment.

Candidates with broader public-sector experience or a combination of public- and private-sector leadership experience are encouraged to apply, provided they possess the relevant financial and governance expertise.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This position offers the opportunity to work directly with a business-minded CAO, influence strategic decision-making, and make a meaningful contribution to one of Alberta's most economically significant municipalities.
The Municipality offers a competitive executive compensation package, including a cost-of-living allowance and relocation assistance if necessary.

At Aplin — together with our brands CompuStaff, Impact Recruitment, and Vantix Systems — we connect great people with great organizations across North America. We believe diverse teams build stronger companies, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We use AI tools to assist in a fair and efficient matching process, helping our recruiters connect the right people with the right opportunities. To be considered, applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada, including holding any required permits. Our recruitment services are always free for job seekers. Accommodation is available upon request throughout all stages of the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance - St. Francis Xavier University
jobs.description:
St. Francis Xavier University is located in Mi’kma’ki, the ancestral and unceded territory of the Mi’kmaw people. We honour their enduring stewardship and commit to advancing reconciliation through learning, reflection and action. We are all Treaty People.

St. Francis Xavier University (StFX) is one of Canada's leading primarily undergraduate universities, recognized for excellence in teaching, research, community engagement, and student success. Located in Antigonish, Nova Scotia, StFX offers an immersive learning environment through its Faculties of Arts, Science, and Education; the Gerald Schwartz School of Business; the Rankin School of Nursing; and the Coady Institute. Home to approximately 5,000 students, 250 faculty members, and 460 staff, the University is supported by an engaged global alumni network of more than 50,000. StFX is known for fostering intellectual growth, leadership, service, and lifelong connections while advancing its commitment to community development and social justice.

StFX is seeking a forward-thinking, inclusive, and collegial leader to serve as its next Vice President (VP), Finance. This is a significant leadership opportunity at an important time for StFX and the Canadian post-secondary sector. Building on a proud tradition, a strong sense of community, and a deeply held commitment to student success, the University is looking to advance its priorities with creativity and focus on emerging opportunities to enhance resilience, invest strategically, and expand the University’s capacity to achieve its goals. The VP will help shape thoughtful, forward-looking choices that strengthen StFX’s long-term position.

Reporting to the President and Vice-Chancellor and serving as a key member of StFX’s executive leadership team, the VP, Finance will provide strategic financial leadership, oversight, and stewardship in support of the University’s academic mission, distinctive student experience, and long-term sustainability. In close partnership with the Academic Vice President and Provost, senior leaders, the Board of Governors and the broader University community, the Vice President will bring an enterprise-wide perspective to financial planning, budgeting, resource allocation, risk, and institutional priorities.

The Vice President leads Financial Services, including Accounts Payable, Financial Reporting, Procurement Services, Student Accounts and Risk Management, and will position the portfolio as a trusted, responsive partner to the University. Combining strong financial acumen with integrity, sound judgment and a collaborative approach, they will advance modernization, evidence-based decisions, and service excellence, while empowering a high-performing team.

The successful candidate will bring senior financial leadership experience in complex organizations, with a track record of improving financial performance, and a post-secondary education in finance, business or a relevant discipline. A Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation is required. Higher education experience and experience in a unionized environment is an asset. The VP combines strong financial acumen across strategy, capital planning, cash flow, treasury, debt and risk with sound knowledge of accounting, fund accounting, financial reporting, controls and governance. Knowledge of post-secondary reporting requirements and government funding is preferred. They will have demonstrated success leading change, improving operations, advising executives and boards, communicating complex matters clearly, and building trust across diverse stakeholder groups. Experience supporting collective bargaining, complex contracts, government funding, partnerships or asset strategy is an asset.

To learn more about St. Francis Xavier University, please visit: https://www.stfx.ca/

StFX is committed to upholding the values of equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility. position plays a critical role in advancing the company's IT business strategy. Acting as the primary liaison between IT and the business, responsible for North America

Proven experience defining and executing regional IT strategies and roadmaps aligned with global IT direction

Experience managing IT budgets, vendor relationships, and service performance

Understanding of technology roadmapping, portfolio management, and demand prioritization

jobs.description:
Full-Time Position: Director of Finance
Location: Hillside Pines Home for Special Care, Bridgewater, NS
Industry: Not-for-Profit, Long Term Care

Hillside Pines has an immediate opening for a Director of Finance. Hillside Pines is a person-first long-term care facility located in the beautiful South Shore area of Nova Scotia. Nestled in the heart of Bridgewater, we offer opportunities for meaningful work as part of a team creating the future of long-term care.

Position Summary
Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the Director of Finance will lead the home’s finance function while serving as a trusted business partner to senior leadership. This role combines strategic leadership with operational oversight and will play a key role in shaping the home’s financial future.

The successful candidate will oversee financial planning, maintenance of accounting, payroll and budgeting systems, including financial management, financial reporting, internal control, budgeting, and forecasting. In addition, they are responsible for ensuring accurate and timely production of statements and analysis to keep Hillside Pines on target financially and within budget.

Key Responsibilities
• Oversee all financial operations, including budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and cash flow management.
• Ensure accurate accounting records, internal controls, and compliance with generally accepted accounting principles, government regulations, and funding requirements.
• Prepare and present monthly financial statements and analysis to the CEO and Board of Directors.
• Lead the annual budgeting process and coordinate year-end audits and external reporting requirements.
• Oversee payroll administration, employee benefit programs, pension contributions, and statutory remittances.
• Manage resident billing, trust accounts, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and capital project accounting.
• Ensure compliance with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Workers' Compensation Board (WCB), insurance, and other regulatory obligations.
• Develop and maintain financial, payroll, and administrative policies and procedures.
• Collaborate with leaders across the organization to support operational planning, financial stewardship, and continuous improvement initiatives.
• Participate as a member of the senior leadership team and support the organization's mission, values, and commitment to quality care.

Requirements
What We’re Looking For
• Bachelor's degree in accounting or business administration.
• CPA designation, active and in good standing (preferred but not mandatory)
• Must be bondable and able to provide relevant documents
• Minimum of 5+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership responsibility.
• Advanced knowledge of Sage 300 computerized accounting programs, and other software programs related to payroll (Payworks), Microsoft Word and Excel.
• Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and business partnering.
• Solid understanding of accounting operations, financial reporting, internal controls, and cash management.
• Demonstrated success leading process improvements, systems implementations, or automation initiatives.
• Experience partnering with senior leadership and/or a Board of Directors.
• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with a collaborative approach and the ability to thrive in a team-focused workplace.
• Proven ability to thrive in a busy and sometimes high-pressure office setting while working independently and meeting deadlines.
• Ensures the privacy and dignity of residents, families and staff are protected and information treated in confidence.

Hours of Work - Monday to Friday 8-4 with occasional evenings related to elder functions.
Work Location – In Person

Hiring Manager’s Note - We’re looking for someone who is both strategic and hands-on — a finance leader who wants to understand how the Home operates, build strong relationships across the leadership team, and help shape the next chapter of financial and operational growth within the Home.

How to Apply
Please email your current resume and salary expectations to: Elizabeth Eberendu, CEO at ceo@hillsidepines.com

jobs.title: Director - Finance, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
About The Foundation

At the St. Joseph’s Health Centre Foundation we are committed to continuing to transform St. Joe’s as a leading community hospital that delivers the best care experiences to Toronto’s west end. We are guided by our mission to inspire philanthropy from our community and raise the funds needed to support that transformation.

St. Joe’s has provided care for millions of people in Toronto’s west end for more than a century. Today it is one Canada’s busiest community teaching hospitals, looking after a vibrant community of over half a million.

The Foundation has grown in recent years to be a leading community hospital foundation with a strong and engaged board of directors. We are looking for a new team member to help with gift management and donor engagement that helps to deliver the best care possible for our community.

About The Position

The Director, Finance, Data & Analytics provides strategic and operational leadership across financial management, business intelligence, fundraising analytics and organizational performance for the Foundation.

As the Foundation enters an ambitious next phase of campaign growth, this role will be responsible for ensuring that the organization has the financial discipline, data infrastructure and insights required to support informed decision-making and maximize fundraising performance.

Working closely with the President & CEO, VP, Operations, Senior Leadership Team and fundraising leaders, the Director will connect financial and fundraising data to provide a clear, timely and actionable view of organizational and campaign performance.

The Director will be the Foundation’s lead resource for financial reporting, fundraising analytics, campaign intelligence, data quality and performance reporting, ensuring that leaders have the information they need to identify opportunities, manage risk, allocate resources and achieve campaign objectives.

The successful candidate will combine strong financial expertise with an analytical and business-oriented mindset, an understanding of fundraising and donor data, and the ability to translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Management
Lead the Foundation’s financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and reporting processes.
Prepare timely, accurate decision-useful financial reports for the President & CEO, Senior Leadership Team, Finance Committee and Board.
Monitor financial performance against budget and provide analysis of material variances, trends, risks and opportunities.
Lead the annual budgeting and collaborate on the business planning process with the VP, Operations and Senior Leadership Team.
Oversee cash flow, investments, receivables, payables and other core financial management activities.
Lead the annual audit and maintain strong financial controls, policies and procedures.
Ensure appropriate financial oversight of designated funds, restricted gifts, commitments and disbursements.
Work closely with external accounting and investment partners as required.
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, regulatory requirements and Foundation policies.
Campaign & Fundraising Analytics
Own the development and ongoing management of the Foundation’s campaign reporting and fundraising analytics framework.
Partner with fundraising leadership to establish clear definitions, methodologies and performance measures for campaign pipeline, proposals, asks, commitments and revenue.
Develop and maintain campaign dashboards that provide management and Board-level visibility into campaign progress and future potential.
Provide analysis that identifies emerging gaps, opportunities and trends and supports proactive campaign management.
Develop forecasting models to support campaign revenue projections and scenario planning.
Work with fundraising leaders to assess portfolio capacity, prospect movement and pipeline sufficiency.
Translate fundraising data into concise insights and recommendations for the Senior Leadership Team, Campaign Leadership, Finance Committee and Board.
Data Strategy, Quality & Business Intelligence
Serve as the Foundation’s internal lead for data strategy, data governance and business intelligence.
Establish standards for data quality, consistency, definitions and reporting across financial and fundraising systems and oversee implantation with Database Manager.
Partner with fundraising and operations teams to improve the use of Raiser's Edge NXT and other systems as strategic management tools.
Identify opportunities to automate reporting and improve data accessibility.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools using appropriate business intelligence platforms.
Connect financial, fundraising, donor and operational data to provide a more complete picture of organizational performance.
Establish appropriate data governance, privacy, security and access practices in partnership with organizational leadership.
Identify technology and systems improvements that will increase efficiency, insight and fundraising productivity.
Prospect & Donor Intelligence
Support the fundraising team with data-driven prospect identification, qualification and prioritization.
Develop reporting to help assess prospect capacity, relationship activity, portfolio composition and movement through the fundraising cycle.
Partner with fundraising leadership to identify gaps in prospect pipelines and opportunities for portfolio development.
Support analysis of donor behaviour, giving patterns, retention, upgrades and other trends that inform fundraising strategy.
Organizational Performance & Decision Support
Working with VP, Operations develop a consistent framework of organizational KPIs aligned with the Foundation’s strategic and business plans.
Provide analysis to support resource allocation, staffing decisions, event and program performance, fundraising investments and operational planning.
Identify trends and insights across revenue, expenses, fundraising activity and organizational performance.
Prepare clear, concise analysis and visualizations for leadership and Board audiences.
Act as a strategic thought partner to leaders, moving beyond reporting results to helping the organization understand what the data means and what action it should inform.
Leadership, Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
Lead continuous improvement of financial and fundraising reporting processes.
Provide leadership and coaching to the administration team, including the Database Manager.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, automate repetitive activities and improve organizational efficiency.
Contribute to a culture of accountability, curiosity, continuous learning and evidence-informed decision-making.
Provide leadership and coaching to staff, contractors or external resources supporting finance, data and analytics.

Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation.
7+ years of progressive experience in finance, financial management, analytics, business intelligence or a related field.
Experience working in a nonprofit, healthcare, fundraising or similarly complex environment is an asset.
Demonstrated experience developing budgets, forecasts, financial models and management reporting.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into clear business insights.
Experience with CRM and fundraising databases; experience with Raiser's Edge NXT is an asset.
Experience developing dashboards and reporting using tools such as Power BI or equivalent is an asset.
Experience working with large or complex datasets and improving data quality and reporting processes.
Strong understanding of data governance, privacy and information management.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to present financial and analytical information clearly.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strategic, curious and improvement-oriented.

At Tangerine, we’re redefining banking. As Canada’s leading digital bank, we thrive on innovation, agility, and bold thinking, tackling every challenge head-on with leading technology and the unstoppable power of collaboration.

Our client-obsessed teams deliver flexible, accessible banking solutions, breakthrough products, and award-winning service. Beyond banking, we’re committed to making an impact in the communities we serve and across our organization. We foster a culture built on integrity, inclusion, and fearless ambition – where diverse perspectives are valued, and people are empowered to do their best work.

Are you ready to disrupt the status quo? Do you crave challenges that push boundaries? If you’re a high performer looking to accelerate your career and reimagine the banking landscape, this is your moment.

Let’s shape the future of banking together!

What You Will Be Doing

The Director, Wealth Strategy & Research will lead the development and execution of strategic initiatives that shape the future of our wealth offerings. This role carries enterprise-level accountability, executive decision support, and stakeholder influence across the organization. The Director will serve as a thought leader, driving insights that inform product strategy, market positioning, and long-term growth.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be:

Define and execute the Tangerine Wealth product roadmap in alignment with business strategic objectives.
Provide strategic insights and recommendations to senior executives, influencing enterprise priorities and business decisions.
Represent Tangerine Wealth in executive forums and prepare board reports, C-suite briefings, and steering-committee updates.
Work closely with market research and competitive intelligence teams to identify actionable insights to inform product development and business decisions.
Continuously monitor the traditional wealth, digital wealth, and fintech landscape for emerging trends, competitor moves, regulatory developments, and technology innovations.
Translate research findings into actionable strategies that drive innovation and client-centric solutions.
Develop and manage structured frameworks for competitor benchmarking, client segmentation, pricing, and go-to-market strategies.
Build data-driven business cases for new initiatives, products, or partnerships.
Support annual and multi-year strategic planning cycles with market input, scenario analysis, and post-implementation reviews to capture lessons learned.
Establish KPIs, scorecards, and dashboards to track progress against strategic objectives.
Maintain decision-support tools and intelligence repositories for timely stakeholder updates.
Produce thought-leadership pieces, white papers, and briefing notes to inform executives and strengthen external positioning.
Distill complex research and analysis into clear recommendations, dashboards, and strategic presentations for senior leadership.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior leaders, cross-functional teams, and external partners, and coordinate input for major decisions to ensure alignment between insights, strategy, and execution.
Champion process optimization, knowledge-sharing, and adoption of best practices by creating templates, playbooks, and standardized deliverables for strategy projects.
Lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering collaboration, empowerment, and continuous improvement.
Championing a client- obsessed culture
Leveraging a growth mindset, embracing learning and continuous improvement
Contributing to a dynamic workplace fostering trust, integrity and inclusion
Removing obstacles to drive momentum across teams
Leading a high performing team through times of change
Supporting teams through transformation activities

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

AI fluency
A craving to contribute to a high-performing team
Ability to drive results in periods of change
Track record of fostering an inclusive culture
10+ years in strategy, research, corporate development, or management consulting, ideally within financial services or fintech.
Strong quantitative and qualitative research capabilities, with deep expertise in the North American wealth management space.
Proven ability to translate insights into actionable strategies and drive cross-functional alignment.
Excellent executive-level communication and presentation skills, with comfort working under tight deadlines on high-visibility projects.
Highly organized, self-directed, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-changing environment.

What's in it for you?

You will be part of a diverse, inclusive, and purpose driven community of client- obsessed innovators who move fast, push boundaries, and celebrate big together.
We are creating something game changing and you get to make your mark on it.
You will have access to thousands of online and in person learning experiences at your fingertips to elevate your career and accelerate your development.
From competitive benefits to programs that support your wellbeing and financial goals- we invest in you today and in your future.*
Tangerine employees participate in Scotiabank’s pension & benefits programs (available to permanent employees)

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

What You Will Be Doing

The Director, Wealth Strategy & Research will lead the development and execution of strategic initiatives that shape the future of our wealth offerings. This role carries enterprise-level accountability, executive decision support, and stakeholder influence across the organization. The Director will serve as a thought leader, driving insights that inform product strategy, market positioning, and long-term growth.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be:

Define and execute the Tangerine Wealth product roadmap in alignment with business strategic objectives.
Provide strategic insights and recommendations to senior executives, influencing enterprise priorities and business decisions.
Represent Tangerine Wealth in executive forums and prepare board reports, C-suite briefings, and steering-committee updates.
Work closely with market research and competitive intelligence teams to identify actionable insights to inform product development and business decisions.
Continuously monitor the traditional wealth, digital wealth, and fintech landscape for emerging trends, competitor moves, regulatory developments, and technology innovations.
Translate research findings into actionable strategies that drive innovation and client-centric solutions.
Develop and manage structured frameworks for competitor benchmarking, client segmentation, pricing, and go-to-market strategies.
Build data-driven business cases for new initiatives, products, or partnerships.
Support annual and multi-year strategic planning cycles with market input, scenario analysis, and post-implementation reviews to capture lessons learned.
Establish KPIs, scorecards, and dashboards to track progress against strategic objectives.
Maintain decision-support tools and intelligence repositories for timely stakeholder updates.
Produce thought-leadership pieces, white papers, and briefing notes to inform executives and strengthen external positioning.
Distill complex research and analysis into clear recommendations, dashboards, and strategic presentations for senior leadership.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior leaders, cross-functional teams, and external partners, and coordinate input for major decisions to ensure alignment between insights, strategy, and execution.
Champion process optimization, knowledge-sharing, and adoption of best practices by creating templates, playbooks, and standardized deliverables for strategy projects.
Lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering collaboration, empowerment, and continuous improvement.
Championing a client- obsessed culture
Leveraging a growth mindset, embracing learning and continuous improvement
Contributing to a dynamic workplace fostering trust, integrity and inclusion
Removing obstacles to drive momentum across teams
Leading a high performing team through times of change
Supporting teams through transformation activities
